metadata.title: Claude, Equity Research.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude's equity-research skill draws on trained financial judgment or a written instruction file, using the skill's own stated purpose as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that Claude only runs the steps that are written down.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (ask Claude to research one company: it opens SKILL.md and runs four steps into one snapshot; ask the same skill something the file doesn't cover, like whether to buy the stock, and no step lights up - not refusal, just nothing written for it)

beats.narration_text: Ask Claude to do equity research, and it's easy to picture a trained analyst inside the model. It isn't — it's a written file Claude reads before acting. Liam explains what that file does.

beats.narration_text: A Claude Skill is a folder Claude reads before it works — not a specialized model, not extra training. This one is called equity-research, and it's one file: a SKILL.md written in plain language, telling Claude to combine analyst consensus estimates, company fundamentals, historical prices, and macro context into a research snapshot.

shot.new_visual_element: An equity-research folder holding one file, SKILL.md; an arrow to four source chips — consensus estimates, fundamentals, historical prices, macro context

production_viz.label: A folder, one file
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon labelled 'equity-research' holds a single card, 'SKILL.md', in teal. An arrow points from it to four small chips that fade in one at a time on the right: consensus estimates, fundamentals, historical prices, macro context. Caption: plain language, no hidden logic.

beats.narration_text: Here's the concrete case: ask Claude to research one company. It opens the SKILL.md and runs the steps in order — pull the analyst consensus estimates, pull the fundamentals, pull the historical prices, pull the macro context — then assembles all four into one snapshot and hands it back. Same steps, every time, for any company you name.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — a request card into SKILL.md; four step-cards light up teal in sequence; arrows converge into one snapshot card

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — one company, four steps
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A card reading 'research this company' arrows into 'SKILL.md'. Above, four step cards — consensus estimates, fundamentals, historical prices, macro context — light up teal one by one in sequence. Arrows from each converge down into a single 'one snapshot' card. THIS EXACT FOUR-STEP SEQUENCE RETURNS AT B03, this time with a fifth question that lights nothing.

beats.narration_text: Ask that same skill a different kind of question — should you buy the stock — and nothing happens, because no step says to answer that. That's not Claude refusing to think; it's this file not covering it. And the reverse holds too: a clean snapshot doesn't mean the numbers were checked or judged — the file only assembled what its steps say to pull.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — a 'should I buy it?' card into SKILL.md, a dashed line to an empty card labelled no step written for it; a clean-snapshot card beside a struck-through 'checked? judged?'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — a question with no step
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 SEQUENCE RETURNS: the same SKILL.md card, this time fed the question 'should I buy it?'. A dashed line leads to an empty, unlit card. Italic caption in terracotta: 'no step written for it.' Beneath: 'not Claude refusing — this file just never wrote it down.' A divider, then the reverse case: a teal 'clean snapshot' card beside the phrase 'checked? judged?' struck through in terracotta, captioned 'only assembled — the file never claims to check the numbers.'

beats.narration_text: Equity-research isn't a trained analyst inside Claude — it's a written file of steps, and Claude only runs the steps that are written down.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I want a comprehensive equity research snapshot for a company I follow — combining analyst consensus estimates, fundamentals, historical prices, and macro context. Read the equity-research skill first, and walk me through what you'll do before you do it. Watch whether it names each step before running — that's the file doing the deciding, not a hidden judgment call. Liam, in for Bear.
